note: Ps57 shadow-of-your-wings (corrected; the cave). Human IB: the refuge-taking (chasah x2) soul under God's wings; cry to God Most High; the endangered nefesh among lions + bowed down; the steadfast (nakon) heart (doubled); roused 'Awake, my GLORY' (kavod = the psalmist's own soul/self) -> sing+make-melody+give-thanks+sing-praises among the nations. God-qualifiers=15 (mercy x2, purpose, send/save/shame/send-out chesed+faithfulness v3, the doxological refrain exalted+glory v5/v11, chesed+faithfulness v10). NB: v8 'my glory'=human char; v5/v11 'your glory'=God qualifier. Lion/weapon/net/pit imagery + cave superscription = standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: take refuge (chasah - my soul takes refuge)
restated as sheltering in the shadow of his wings

'for in you my soul takes REFUGE (chasah)' — the fugitive's flight to God; chasah (to seek shelter) the soul's turning to God as its hiding-place, resting on his mercy (v1, the qualifier) — trust as taking cover in a person
take refuge (chasah - in the shadow of your wings I will take refuge)
in the shadow of God's wings
till the storms of destruction pass by
the same refuge-taking, now under his wings

'in the shadow of your wings I will TAKE REFUGE (chasah), till the storms of destruction pass by' — the vivid image of sheltering under God like a bird's young beneath its wings; chasah here the deliberate, patient hiding in God until danger passes — refuge that waits out the storm
cry out / call (qara - I cry out to God Most High)
to God who fulfils his purpose for him and sends his love to save (v2-3)

'I CRY OUT (qara) to God Most High, to God who fulfils his purpose for me' — the confident appeal from the cave; qara here the cry to the Most High, resting on God's committed purpose (the qualifier) — a plea that already trusts the outcome, that God will send love and faithfulness to save
trample / pant after (shaaph - him who tramples on me)
whom God will put to shame (v3)

'he will put to shame him who TRAMPLES (shaaph) on me' — the hounding foe (same verb as Ps56); shaaph the enemy who pants to crush the psalmist, whom God will shame (the qualifier) — the trampler overthrown by the God who is exalted
soul / life (nefesh - my soul is in the midst of lions)
in the midst of fiery lions
the same nefesh bowed down by their trap (v6)

'My SOUL (nefesh) is in the midst of lions' — the self surrounded by ravening foes; nefesh here the psalmist's life among man-beasts whose teeth are spears and tongues are swords — the endangered soul that nonetheless takes refuge under God's wings
soul / life (nefesh - my soul was bowed down)
bowed down by the enemies' net
the soul that was among lions (v4)

'they set a net for my steps; my SOUL (nefesh) was bowed down' — the self dejected under the enemies' trap; nefesh here bowed low with distress — yet the pit they dug becomes their own grave, and the bowed soul rises to a steadfast heart (v7)
steadfast, fixed (nakon), said twice for emphasis
issues in singing and making melody

'My HEART (leb) is STEADFAST (nakon), O God, my heart is steadfast!' — the fixed, unwavering inner core, declared twice; leb here the heart set firm on God amid lions and traps — the opposite of the bowed-down soul (v6), resolve that breaks into song
sing (shir - I will sing and make melody)
rousing his glory, harp, lyre, and the dawn
praising the God who is to be exalted above the heavens (v5)

'I will SING (shir) and make melody!' — the steadfast heart overflowing in song; shir here praise that flows from settled resolve, calling on God to be exalted above the heavens (v5, the qualifier) — worship born of confidence, not yet of deliverance
make melody / sing praise (zamar - and make melody)

'I will sing and MAKE MELODY (zamar)!' — the instrumental praise twinned with song; zamar here the music of the roused heart, summoning harp and lyre and even the dawn to join the praise of the steadfast soul
glory (kavod - Awake, my glory! = the soul/self)
rousing harp, lyre, and the dawn
the self that sings and gives thanks (v7,9)

'AWAKE, my GLORY (kavod)!' — the psalmist rousing his own inmost self to praise; kavod here 'my glory' = the soul/noblest part of the person (not God's glory, which is v5/v11) — the inner self summoned from dejection (v6) to sing before the dawn
give thanks (yadah - I will give thanks among the peoples)
to the Lord, among the peoples
paired with singing praises among the nations
because God's steadfast love is great to the heavens (v10)

'I will GIVE THANKS (yadah) to you, O Lord, among the peoples' — praise carried out to the nations; yadah here thanksgiving that will not stay private but proclaims God among the peoples, moved by his steadfast love great to the heavens (v10, the qualifier)
sing praises (zamar - I will sing praises among the nations)
paired with giving thanks among the peoples
because God's faithfulness reaches to the clouds (v10)

'I will SING PRAISES (zamar) to you among the nations' — praise made public and universal; zamar here the singing that answers God's faithfulness reaching to the clouds (v10, the qualifier) — the delivered heart wanting all peoples to know God's greatness
be merciful / gracious (chanan - be merciful to me)
God's mercy, the ground of the soul's refuge (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's mercy): 'Be MERCIFUL (chanan) to me, O God' - God's graciousness is not a human IB char; the divine favour the psalmist's refuge-taking soul (280347) rests on. Qualifier.
be merciful (chanan - be merciful to me, doubled)
God's mercy appealed to a second time (v1)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's mercy, doubled): 'be MERCIFUL (chanan) to me' - the emphatic repeat of the appeal to God's grace, on which the soul takes refuge (280347). Qualifier.
fulfil / complete (gamar - who fulfills his purpose for me)
God fulfils his purpose for the one who cries to him (v2)

v2 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'to God who FULFILS (gamar) his purpose for me' - God's completing of his purpose is not a human IB char; the committed divine intent the psalmist's cry (280372) relies on. Qualifier.
send (shalach - he will send from heaven and save)
God sends from heaven to save the one who cries (v3)
v3 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'He will SEND (shalach) from heaven and save me' - God's sending is not a human IB char; the heavenly rescue answering the cry (280372). Qualifier.
God saves the one who cries to him (v3)
v3 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'and SAVE (yasha) me' - God's saving is not a human IB char; the deliverance the cry (280372) counts on. Qualifier.
put to shame / reproach (charaph - put to shame him who tramples)
God puts the trampler to shame (v3)
v3 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'he will put to SHAME (charaph) him who tramples on me' - God's shaming of the enemy is not a human IB char; the judgment on the trampler (280385). Qualifier.
send out (shalach - God will send out his love and faithfulness)
God sends out his love and faithfulness to the one who cries (v3)

v3 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'God will SEND OUT (shalach) his steadfast love and his faithfulness' - God's sending of his covenant attributes is not a human IB char; the rescue meeting the cry (280372). Qualifier.
God's love sent to save the one who cries (v3)
v3 QUALIFIER (God's chesed): 'God will send out his STEADFAST LOVE (chesed)' - God's covenant love is not a human IB char; the saving attribute God sends to the crying psalmist (280372). Qualifier.
God's faithfulness sent to save the one who cries (v3)
v3 QUALIFIER (God's faithfulness): 'and his FAITHFULNESS (emet)' - God's reliability is not a human IB char; the covenant attribute God sends with his love to save (280372). Qualifier.
be exalted / high (rum - be exalted above the heavens)
the doxology the psalmist's singing ascribes to God (v5)

v5 QUALIFIER (God's exaltation): 'Be EXALTED (rum), O God, above the heavens!' - God's being lifted high is not a human IB char; the supremacy the psalmist's praise (280430) ascribes to God, the refrain framing the psalm (v5, v11). Qualifier.
glory (kavod - let your glory be over all the earth)
God's glory the psalmist's praise desires over all the earth (v5)

v5 QUALIFIER (God's glory): 'Let your GLORY (kavod) be over all the earth!' - God's glory (distinct from 'my glory'=the soul, v8) is not a human IB char; the divine splendour the psalmist's praise (280430) longs to see fill the earth. Qualifier.
steadfast love (chesed - great to the heavens)
God's love, great to the heavens, ground of the thanksgiving (v10)

v10 QUALIFIER (God's chesed): 'For your STEADFAST LOVE (chesed) is great to the heavens' - God's covenant love is not a human IB char; its cosmic vastness grounds the psalmist's thanksgiving among the peoples (280439). Qualifier.
God's faithfulness, reaching the clouds, ground of the praise (v10)

v10 QUALIFIER (God's faithfulness): 'your FAITHFULNESS (emet) to the clouds' - God's reliability is not a human IB char; its sky-high reach grounds the psalmist's singing praises among the nations (280442). Qualifier.
be exalted (rum - be exalted above the heavens)
the closing doxology the psalmist's praise ascribes to God (v11)

v11 QUALIFIER (God's exaltation): 'Be EXALTED (rum), O God, above the heavens!' - God's supremacy is not a human IB char; the refrain closing the psalm, the summit of the psalmist's praise (280442). Qualifier.
glory (kavod - let your glory be over all the earth)
God's glory the psalmist's praise desires over all the earth (v11)

v11 QUALIFIER (God's glory): 'Let your GLORY (kavod) be over all the earth!' - God's glory is not a human IB char; the closing refrain, the object of the psalmist's universal praise (280442). Qualifier.
flee (barach - when he fled from Saul)
superscription: 'when he FLED (barach) from Saul, in the cave' - the historical flight framing the psalm; an external event in the heading, not the psalm's inner-being content. Standalone.
superscription: 'in the CAVE (mearah)' - the setting of the psalm's composition; a place, part of the historical heading. Standalone.

v1: 'in you my SOUL (nefesh) takes refuge' - the bearer of the refuge-taking; the refuge-act is the char (280347, bearer=soul), here the soul-noun itself. Standalone (the refuge-bearer, captured in 280347).
v1: 'in the SHADOW (tsel) of your wings' - the image of God's protective covering; the sheltering is the char (280351), here the metaphor of the shadow. Standalone (image of God's protection).
v1: 'the shadow of your WINGS (kanaph)' - the image of God as a bird sheltering its young; the refuge is the char (280351), here the wing-metaphor. Standalone (image of God's protection).
destruction / engulfing ruin (havvah - storms of destruction)
v1: 'till the storms of DESTRUCTION (havvah) pass by' - the calamity the psalmist shelters from; the external threat (recurs Ps52,55), the danger the refuge waits out. Standalone (the calamity).
pass by / pass over (abar - till it pass by)
v1: 'till the storms of destruction PASS BY (abar)' - the passing of the calamity the refuge waits for; the temporal limit of the sheltering (280351), not an inner operation. Standalone.
lions (labi - in the midst of lions)
v4: 'My soul is in the midst of LIONS (labi)' - the enemies imaged as ravening beasts; the endangered soul is the char (280392), here the lion-image of the foes. Standalone (image).
lie down (shakab - I lie down amid fiery beasts)

v4: 'I LIE DOWN (shakab) amid those who breathe fire' - the psalmist's plight, forced to rest among deadly foes; his situation, captured with the endangered-soul char (280392). Standalone (his plight).
v4: 'amid those who breathe FIRE (lahat)' - the enemies as fire-breathing beasts; the beast-image of the foes, not an inner operation. Standalone (image).
v4: 'whose TEETH (shen) are spears and arrows' - the enemies' teeth imaged as weapons; the weapon-catalogue of the foes' menace. Standalone (image).
v4: 'their teeth are SPEARS (chanit)' - the weapon-image of the enemies' devouring; part of the beast/weapon catalogue. Standalone (image).
v4: 'spears and ARROWS (chets)' - the weapon-image of the enemies' teeth; part of the menace-catalogue. Standalone (image).
tongues (lashon - whose tongues are sharp swords)
v4: 'whose TONGUES (lashon) are sharp swords' - the enemies' cutting speech imaged as blades; the tongue-as-weapon image (cf Ps55,64), the vehicle of their menace. Standalone (image).
v4: 'sharp (chad) swords' - the keenness of the tongue-as-sword image; part of the weapon-catalogue. Standalone (image).
v4: 'their tongues are sharp SWORDS (chereb)' - the tongue-as-sword image closing the weapon-catalogue of the enemies' menace. Standalone (image).
set / prepare (kun - they set a net)
v6: 'They SET (kun) a net for my steps' - the enemies' act of laying a trap; the entrapment scheme, its reversal the point (they fell in). Standalone (the trap-setting).
net (resheth - a net for my steps)
v6: 'a NET (resheth) for my steps' - the trap the enemies laid; the image of their scheme against him. Standalone (image/trap).
steps (paam - a net for my steps)
v6: 'a net for my STEPS (paam)' - the psalmist's path, the object the trap targeted; not an inner operation. Standalone (the steps).
bow down / cast down (kaphaph - my soul was bowed down)
v6: 'my soul was BOWED DOWN (kaphaph)' - the dejection of the soul; the being-bowed carried in the endangered-soul char (280416). Standalone (the bowing).
v6: 'They DUG (karah) a pit in my way' - the enemies' act of preparing a snare, into which they themselves fell; the entrapment scheme. Standalone (the trap-digging).
pit (shichah - a pit in my way)
v6: 'a PIT (shichah) in my way' - the snare the enemies dug, image of their scheme and (reversed) their own doom. Standalone (image/trap).
fall (naphal - they have fallen into it)
v6: 'but they have FALLEN (naphal) into it themselves' - the poetic-justice reversal, the enemies caught in their own pit; an outcome of judgment, not an inner operation. Standalone (the reversal).
steadfast / fixed (nakon - my heart is steadfast)
v7: 'my heart is STEADFAST (nakon)' - the fixedness/firmness of the heart; the quality carried in the steadfast-heart char (280424). Standalone (the quality).
heart (leb - my heart is steadfast, repeated)
v7: 'my HEART (leb) is steadfast!' - the emphatic repeat of the steadfast-heart declaration (280424); the doubling stressing the firm resolve, carried in that char. Standalone (emphatic repeat).
steadfast / fixed (nakon - my heart is steadfast, repeated)
v7: the repeated 'STEADFAST (nakon)' in the doubled declaration; the firmness of the heart (280424), stated twice for emphasis. Standalone (the quality, repeat).
v8: 'AWAKE (ur), my glory!' - the summons rousing the psalmist's own soul to praise; the roused self is the char (280433), here the rousing-call. Standalone (the rousing summons).
awake / rouse (ur - Awake, O harp and lyre!)
v8: 'AWAKE (ur), O harp and lyre!' - the summons rousing the instruments to join the praise; part of the call to worship, addressed to the harp and lyre. Standalone (rousing the instruments).
awake / rouse (ur - I will awake the dawn)
v8: 'I will AWAKE (ur) the dawn!' - the psalmist's praise so eager it rouses the morning itself; the pre-dawn worship, a vivid figure of the roused self (280433). Standalone (rousing the dawn).
dawn (shachar - I will awake the dawn)
v8: 'I will awake the DAWN (shachar)' - the morning the psalmist's praise anticipates and rouses; the image of praise beginning before daybreak. Standalone (image).
clouds / skies (shachaq - your faithfulness to the clouds)
v10: 'your faithfulness to the CLOUDS (shachaq)' - the cosmic measure of God's faithfulness; the sky as the yardstick of its vastness, a spatial image. Standalone (cosmic measure).
